arxiv-2301-05841.title: Distributed Optimal Formation Control for an Uncertain Multiagent System in the Plane Thanks: 1 C. Enwerem and J. Baras are with the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering and the Institute for Systems Research, University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742, USA. Thanks: 2 D. Romero is wit
arxiv-2301-05841.creator: Clinton Enwerem, John Baras, Danilo Romero
arxiv-2301-05841.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a distributed optimal multiagent control scheme for quadrotor formation tracking under localization errors. Our control architecture is based on a leader-follower approach, where a single leader quadrotor tracks a desired trajectory while the followers maintain their relative positions in a triangular formation.

arxiv-2311-03387.title: Determination of droplet size from wide-angle light scattering image data using convolutional neural networks
arxiv-2311-03387.creator: Tom Kirstein 1 , Simon Aßmann 2 , Orkun Furat 1 , Stefan Will 2 and Volker Schmidt 1
arxiv-2311-03387.description: Abstract Wide-angle light scattering (WALS) offers the possibility of a highly temporally and spatially resolved measurement of droplets in spray-based methods for nanoparticle synthesis. The size of these droplets is a critical variable affecting the final properties of synthesized materials such as hetero-aggregates.

arxiv-2501-19136.title: Effective theory for stochastic particle acceleration, with application to magnetized turbulence
arxiv-2501-19136.creator: Martin Lemoine
arxiv-2501-19136.description: Abstract The physics of particle acceleration in turbulent plasmas is a topic of broad interest, which is making rapid progress thanks to dedicated, large-scale numerical experiments. The first part of this paper presents an effective theory of stochastic Fermi acceleration, which subsumes all forms of non-resonant acceleration in ideal electric fields and is applicable in generic settings.

arxiv-2509-18030.title: RadEval: A framework for radiology text evaluation
arxiv-2509-18030.creator: Justin Xu ♠, &Xi Zhang ♢ &Javid Abderezaei ♡ &Julie Bauml ♡ and Roger Boodoo ♡ &Fatemeh Haghighi ♡ &Ali Ganjizadeh ♡ and Eric Brattain ♡ &Dave Van Veen ♡ &Zaiqiao Meng ♢ and David Eyre ♠ &Jean-Benoit Delbrouck ♡, and ♠ University of Oxford ♢ University of Glasgow ♡ HOPPR justin.xu@ndm.ox.ac.uk, jean
arxiv-2509-18030.description: Abstract We introduce RadEval, a unified, open-source framework for evaluating radiology texts. RadEval consolidates a diverse range of metrics – from classic n - gram overlap (BLEU, ROUGE) and contextual measures (BERTScore) to clinical concept-based scores (F1CheXbert, F1RadGraph, RaTEScore, SRR-BERT, TemporalEntityF1) and advanced LLM - based evaluators (GREEN).

arxiv-2510-17437.title: Multilingual Clinical NER for Diseases and Medications Recognition in Cardiology Texts using BERT Embeddings
arxiv-2510-17437.creator: Manuela Daniela Danu, George Marica, Constantin Suciu, Lucian Mihai Itu, Oladimeji Farri
arxiv-2510-17437.description: Abstract The rapidly increasing volume of electronic health record (EHR) data underscores a pressing need to unlock biomedical knowledge from unstructured clinical texts to support advancements in data-driven clinical systems, including patient diagnosis, disease progression monitoring, treatment effects assessment, prediction of future clinical events, etc.

arxiv-2602-12630.title: TensorCommitments: A Lightweight Verifiable Inference for Language Models
arxiv-2602-12630.creator: Oguzhan Baser, Elahe Sadeghi, Eric Wang, David Ribeiro Alves, Sam Kazemian, Hong Kang, Sandeep P. Chinchali, Sriram Vishwanath
arxiv-2602-12630.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Oguzhan Baser, Elahe Sadeghi, Eric Wang, David Ribeiro Alves, Sam Kazemian, Hong Kang, Sandeep P. Chinchali, Sriram Vishwanath. Most large language models (LLMs) run on external clouds: users send a prompt, pay for inference, and must trust that the remote GPU executes the LLM without any adversarial tampering. We critically ask how to achieve verifiable LLM inference, where a prover (the service) must convince a verifier (the client) that an inference was run correctly without rerunning the LLM.

pmc-10561990.title: An R package for ensemble learning stacking
pmc-10561990.creator: Taichi Nukui, Akio Onogi, Shanfeng Zhu
pmc-10561990.description: SummarySupervised learning is widely used in biology for prediction, and ensemble learning, including stacking, is a promising technique for increasing and stabilizing the prediction accuracy. In this study, we developed an R package for stacking. This package depends on the R package caret and can handle models supported by caret.

pmc-11525582.title: Effects of train speed and passenger capacity on the environmental vibration of viaduct and surrounding soil of suburban railways
pmc-11525582.creator: Hongkai Wang, Dong Li, Jili Yin, Zhimin Li, Zhoujian You, Futong Wang
pmc-11525582.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Compared with the general urban rail transit, some of the current rapid urban rail transit can reach a maximum speed of 140 km/h when the train is running, which exceeds the speed level of the general urban rail transit. To consider the influence of different speeds and loads on the vibration of viaducts and the surrounding soil environment, this paper establishes a three-dimensional finite element model of rail-viaduct soil.

pmc-11612484.title: Study of repulsive permanent magnetic levitation mechanism and its dynamic characteristics
pmc-11612484.creator: Fazhu Zhou, Jie Yang, Hailin Hu, Tao Gao
pmc-11612484.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Permanent magnet magnetic levitation (PMFL) system has the characteristics of zero-power levitation, strong load-carrying capacity and self-stabilization, so it has obvious advantages in the application of rail transportation and heavy-duty transmission and other fields. However, due to the lack of active control of electromagnetism and the existence of multi-point coupling, it is easily affected by external factors, and its dynamic characteristics and its complexity.

pmc-12363044.title: Towards more reliable gambling cost estimates, a population-based study with register-linkage
pmc-12363044.creator: Tiina A Latvala, Matthew Rockloff, Matthew Browne, Tomi Roukka, Tomi P Lintonen, Anne H Salonen
pmc-12363044.description: BackgroundAlthough past research has shown a strong association between gambling participation and harms, relatively few studies have attempted to quantify the cost of these harms to society. The need to quantify costs has been identified in several countries, however, no consensus exists in the field of gambling studies on how one should estimate them.

pmc-13144620.title: The Effect of Gluten-Free Diet on Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Disease Severity of Autistic Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13144620.creator: Maryam Shoaran, Pouya Golshaniniya, Amirhosein Dadashzadeh Asl, Shahram Sadeghvand, Mahsa Valizadeh, Ali Akbari
pmc-13144620.description: Objectives:Autism Sspectrum Disorder (ASD) is a kind of neurodevelopmental disease characterized by difficulties in social interactions, verbal and non-verbal communication, movement limitations, and repetitive movement patterns. The goal of this study is to investigate the effects of a Gluten-Free Diet (GFD) on gastrointestinal (GI) and neurological symptoms in patients diagnosed with autism.

pmc-13558342.title: Bioabsorbable vs. titanium screws in first metatarsophalangeal joint arthrodesis: a pilot randomized controlled trial with 2-year follow-up
pmc-13558342.creator: Nikke Partio, Ville Mattila, Ville Waris, Heikki Mäenpää
pmc-13558342.description: IntroductionTo assess the feasibility and preliminary clinical outcomes of bioabsorbable screw fixation in first metatarsophalangeal joint arthrodesis compared to conventional titanium screw fixation. Methods: In this prospective pilot randomized controlled trial, 30 patients were allocated 1:1 to bioabsorbable or titanium cannulated lag screw fixation. Arthrodesis was performed using a cup-and-cone technique at two Finnish hospitals.

pmc-13637397.title: Association of frailty index with incident complete tooth loss among middle-aged and older Chinese adults: a longitudinal cohort study based on CHARLS
pmc-13637397.creator: Guisheng Luo, Xiaoming Li, Zhen Wang, Qixin Chen
pmc-13637397.description: BackgroundTooth loss is a severe oral health condition among middle-aged and older adults and is associated with impaired mastication, nutritional problems, and reduced quality of life. Frailty—a state of increased vulnerability to adverse health outcomes—may represent an underexplored factor associated with oral health outcomes, but population-based evidence from China remains limited.

uslaw-usc-t42-s300ff87a.title: 42 U.S.C. § 300ff–87a — National HIV/AIDS testing goal
uslaw-usc-t42-s300ff87a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s300ff87a.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 6A (Public Health Service); Subchapter XXIV (Hiv Health Care Services Program); Part E (General Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general Not later than January 1, 2010, the Secretary shall establish a national HIV/AIDS testing goal of 5,000,000 tests for HIV/AIDS annually through federally-supported HIV/AIDS prevention, treatment, and care.
